data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) privacy policy, provides the impetus and foundations for the Privacy Program, and guides the development of associated processes and procedures.
policy_statements.target: United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) privacy policy

policy_statements.source_text: It is USDA policy to comply with Federal requirements to establish, implement, and support a Departmental Privacy Program and associated program plans to continually manage risks to privacy data, Personally Identifiable Information (PII), and USDA’s information resources.
policy_statements.target: Departmental Privacy Program and associated program plans

policy_statements.source_text: This directive establishes USDA policy and compliance with the E-Government Act of 2002, as amended, 44 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 3501; the Confidential Information Protection and Statistical Efficiency Act of 2002, 44 U.S.C. § 3501; the Privacy Act of 1974, 5 U.S.C. § 552 (as amended); the Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 U.S.C. 11101 et seq.; and Office of Management and Budget (OMB) policies and guidance.
cross_references: E-Government Act of 2002, as amended, 44 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 3501
Confidential Information Protection and Statistical Efficiency Act of 2002, 44 U.S.C. § 3501
Privacy Act of 1974, 5 U.S.C. § 552 (as amended)
Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 U.S.C. 11101 et seq.

policy_statements.source_text: This policy supersedes Departmental Manual (DM) 3515-000, Privacy Requirements, dated February 17, 2005.
cross_references: Departmental Manual (DM) 3515-000, Privacy Requirements, dated February 17, 2005

policy_statements.source_text: This policy is effective immediately and remains in effect until superseded or expired.
All USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will align their policies and procedures with this DR within 6 months of the publication date.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: within 6 months of the publication date

policy_statements.source_text: The term “USDA personnel” means USDA employees, contractors, affiliates, interns, fellows, and volunteers who work for, on behalf of, USDA, and whose work is overseen by USDA employees.

This policy applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices and USDA personnel working for, or on behalf of, USDA regarding the collection, use, maintenance, disclosure, deletion, destruction, or dissemination of PII, in transit and at rest, for official purposes and regarding any other activity that impacts the privacy of individuals, as determined by the USDA Senior Agency Official for Privacy (SAOP).
policy_statements.target: all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices and USDA personnel working for, or on behalf of, USDA
conditions: working for, or on behalf of, USDA
in transit and at rest
for official purposes
as determined by the USDA Senior Agency Official for Privacy (SAOP)

policy_statements.source_text: The legal rights of individuals are guaranteed and must be protected regarding the collection, use, maintenance, disclosure, deletion, destruction, or dissemination of PII in compliance with Federal laws, regulations, and policies.
This DR provides direction and guidance to Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices for implementing those requirements.
policy_statements.target: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: The Department will comply with OMB memoranda M-01-05, Guidance on Inter-Agency Sharing of Personal Data – Protecting Personal Privacy; M-03-22, OMB Guidance for Implementing the Privacy Provisions of the E-Government Act of 2002; M-05-08, Designation of Senior Agency Officials for Privacy; M-11-02, Sharing Data While Protecting Privacy; and M-16-24, Role and Designation of Senior Agency Officials for Privacy.
cross_references: M-01-05, Guidance on Inter-Agency Sharing of Personal Data – Protecting Personal Privacy
M-03-22, OMB Guidance for Implementing the Privacy Provisions of the E-Government Act of 2002
M-05-08, Designation of Senior Agency Officials for Privacy
M-11-02, Sharing Data While Protecting Privacy
M-16-24, Role and Designation of Senior Agency Officials for Privacy

policy_statements.source_text: The Department will comply with OMB Circulars A-108, Federal Agency Responsibilities for Review, Reporting, and Publication under the Privacy Act, and A-130, Managing Information as a Strategic Resource, Appendix II: Responsibilities for Managing Personally Identifiable Information, which include the Fair Information Practice Principles, as guidelines for USDA’s privacy policy.
cross_references: A-108, Federal Agency Responsibilities for Review, Reporting, and Publication under the Privacy Act
A-130, Managing Information as a Strategic Resource, Appendix II: Responsibilities for Managing Personally Identifiable Information
Fair Information Practice Principles

policy_statements.source_text: The Department will comply with OMB specific guidance on Privacy management and control requirements, to include the safeguarding of PII, in accordance with OMB memoranda.
policy_statements.target: OMB specific guidance on Privacy management and control requirements

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will coordinate with the Chief Privacy Officer (CPO), or designee, when developing and implementing privacy policy and procedures to ensure they are consistent with Federal laws, regulations, guidance, and Departmental policy.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: when developing and implementing privacy policy and procedures

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will ensure all personnel have received privacy training, and provide support to Departmental leadership on privacy-related matters, data gathering, reporting requirements, and privacy-related investigations and incident reporting.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices , through their Privacy Officers, Privacy Act Officers, Privacy Analysts, and other Privacy Points of Contact (PPOC), will coordinate with the CPO, or designee, to ensure that their processes and procedures follow USDA privacy policy and standards; thereby enhancing the overall consistency of privacy protections across USDA.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: All privacy policies and associated procedures and controls will be reviewed annually and updated, if necessary, within 1 year of the issuance of changes in Federal law, regulations, and OMB and National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) guidance.
policy_statements.target: All privacy policies and associated procedures and controls
conditions: if necessary
within 1 year of the issuance of changes in Federal law, regulations, and OMB and National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) guidance

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices may develop privacy policies, processes, and procedures that meet, or exceed corresponding Departmental policy requirements if needed, to further enhance Departmental privacy policy.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: that meet, or exceed corresponding Departmental policy requirements
if needed

policy_statements.source_text: However, those policies, processes, and procedures will neither contradict, nor be less stringent than, Departmental policy requirements.
The Secretary of Agriculture will:
Ensure that all PII and information systems within which PII is stored, processed, or transits, are protected in compliance with all Federal requirements;
policy_statements.target: all PII and information systems within which PII is stored, processed, or transits
conditions: within which PII is stored, processed, or transits

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that privacy and PII management processes are integrated into USDA’s strategic, operational, budgetary, and acquisition planning processes;
Be accountable for managing the cybersecurity risks to PII maintained by USDA, in both electronic and hard-copy format;
policy_statements.target: cybersecurity risks to PII maintained by USDA
conditions: in both electronic and hard-copy format

policy_statements.source_text: Designate a senior official at the Deputy Assistant Secretary or equivalent level who serves in a central leadership position, that has the necessary skills, knowledge, and expertise to lead, direct, and carry out the privacy-related functions described in law and OMB policies, as the SAOP; and
policy_statements.target: senior official at the Deputy Assistant Secretary or equivalent level
conditions: who serves in a central leadership position
that has the necessary skills, knowledge, and expertise to lead, direct, and carry out the privacy-related functions described in law and OMB policies

policy_statements.source_text: Delegate the necessary authority to the SAOP to carry out all assigned duties.
The USDA CIO will:
Serve as the USDA SAOP;
Serve as the Department’s official point of contact on all matters related to privacy in the Federal Government;
Govern the USDA Privacy Program;
Review and approve USDA’s privacy policy and procedures to ensure they are comprehensive, current, and compliant with applicable privacy laws and Federal guidance;
Be responsible for the overall management of the Department’s Privacy Program portfolio, to include budget management;
Chair the Data Integrity Board (DIB);

Coordinate with the USDA Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) to provide guidance regarding information technology and technology-related programs to develop and implement policies and procedures to safeguard PII used or maintained by the Department, in accordance with Federal law and policy;

Coordinate with the Director, Office of Contracting and Procurement, serving as the Senior Procurement Executive, to ensure that contract provisions related to assisting with a breach and breach notifications are uniform and consistently included in agency contracts;
policy_statements.target: Director, Office of Contracting and Procurement
conditions: related to assisting with a breach and breach notifications

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinate with the Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights on privacy issues related to civil rights and civil liberties arising from Departmental activities, such as collections, privacy violations, PII security incidents, development of policy, procedures, and contract language, as required;
conditions: as required

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure all USDA personnel receive appropriate training and education regarding their privacy protection responsibilities;
Ensure Departmental preparedness for and responding to an incident or breach, to include development, implementation, and testing of a breach response plan;
policy_statements.target: Departmental preparedness for and responding to an incident or breach

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure Departmental, Mission Area, agency, and staff office incident management and breach response plans and procedures are developed, disseminated, fully implemented, and periodically tested (with test results and artifacts documented, analyzed to identify weaknesses, and retained for audit and investigation purposes);
policy_statements.target: Departmental, Mission Area, agency, and staff office incident management and breach response plans and procedures

policy_statements.source_text: Represent USDA at the Federal Privacy Council;
Ensure Departmental development and evaluation of legislative, regulatory, and related policies address privacy issues and involve privacy collaborations, as needed;
policy_statements.target: Departmental development and evaluation of legislative, regulatory, and related policies
conditions: as needed

policy_statements.source_text: Review, approve, and maintain a list of all Departmental information systems that process, store, collect PII, or facilitate the transfer of PII between information systems;
policy_statements.target: all Departmental information systems that process, store, collect PII, or facilitate the transfer of PII between information systems
conditions: that process, store, collect PII, or facilitate the transfer of PII between information systems

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that Federal statutory and regulatory reporting requirements, OMB guidelines, USDA Departmental directives, and other applicable guidance have been met;
policy_statements.target: Federal statutory and regulatory reporting requirements, OMB guidelines, USDA Departmental directives, and other applicable guidance

policy_statements.source_text: Submit applicable reports as required on the USDA Privacy Program; and
conditions: as required

policy_statements.source_text: Designate and appoint the USDA CPO.
The USDA CPO will:
Establish, coordinate implementation, and ensure compliance with USDA Departmental privacy policy and supplemental guidance.
policy_statements.target: USDA Departmental privacy policy and supplemental guidance

policy_statements.source_text: The CPO establishes the privacy policy, subject to review and approval by the CISO, and SAOP;
conditions: subject to review and approval by the CISO, and SAOP

policy_statements.source_text: Evaluate Departmental directives, rulemakings, technologies, policies, procedures, guidelines, programs, projects, and systems (including pilot activities), whether proposed or operational, for potential privacy impacts and advise USDA leadership and Mission Area, agency, and staff office heads on implementing corresponding privacy protections, providing approval as appropriate;
policy_statements.target: Departmental directives, rulemakings, technologies, policies, procedures, guidelines, programs, projects, and systems (including pilot activities)
conditions: whether proposed or operational
as appropriate

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinate with Mission Area, agency, and staff office heads, Privacy Officers, Privacy Act Officers, Privacy Analysts, and other Mission Area, agency, and staff office heads PPOCs to ensure that the Department follows USDA privacy policies, OMB memoranda, applicable privacy laws, and Federal Governmentwide privacy policies regarding protecting PII;
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, and staff office heads, Privacy Officers, Privacy Act Officers, Privacy Analysts, and other Mission Area, agency, and staff office heads PPOCs

policy_statements.source_text: Chair the USDA Privacy Council meetings and ensure adherence to the Privacy Council Charter, forthcoming;
cross_references: Privacy Council Charter, forthcoming

policy_statements.source_text: Serve as the DIB Secretary and ensure adherence to DIB Charter, forthcoming;
cross_references: DIB Charter, forthcoming

policy_statements.source_text: Process privacy complaints from organizations and individuals regarding Departmental activities and ensuring redress is provided, as appropriate;
policy_statements.target: privacy complaints from organizations and individuals regarding Departmental activities
conditions: as appropriate

policy_statements.source_text: Review privacy incidents or matters relating to possible violations of privacy arising from the administration of any Department program or operations;
policy_statements.target: privacy incidents or matters relating to possible violations of privacy arising from the administration of any Department program or operations

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that the Department’s privacy reports are transmitted to OMB and Congress, as applicable;
conditions: as applicable

policy_statements.source_text: Provide technical assistance to system and program managers, as needed, in the development of privacy documentation; and
conditions: as needed

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinate with the USDA CIO, the USDA CISO, and the Director of the Office of Homeland Security (OHS) to provide guidance regarding information technology and technology-related programs to develop and implement policies and procedures to safeguard PII used or maintained by the Department in accordance with Federal law and policy.
policy_statements.target: USDA CIO, the USDA CISO, and the Director of the Office of Homeland Security (OHS)

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA CISO will:
Review and approve Departmental directives and waivers related to privacy protection administration;
policy_statements.target: Departmental directives and waivers related to privacy protection administration

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure the annual Information Security Awareness and Training incorporates provisions for protecting privacy and privacy information;
policy_statements.target: annual Information Security Awareness and Training

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure privacy documentation reviews for Privacy Threshold Analysis (PTA) and Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) are incorporated into the security assessment and authorization process;
policy_statements.target: privacy documentation reviews for Privacy Threshold Analysis (PTA) and Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA)

policy_statements.source_text: Collaborate with CPO on PII practices involving information system security to include, but not limited to, PII breaches, system reviews to include privacy and security controls, and compliance; and
Formulate budget allocations and provide staffing resources for privacy personnel and the CPO, supporting the Departmental Privacy Office.
The Director, Office of Contracting and Procurement, will:
Coordinate with the SAOP to ensure that contract provisions related to assisting with a breach and breach notifications are uniform and consistently included in agency contracts.
policy_statements.actor_name: Director, Office of Contracting and Procurement

policy_statements.source_text: The Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights will:

Coordinate with the SAOP on privacy issues related to civil rights and civil liberties arising from Departmental activities, such as collections, privacy violations, PII security incidents, development of policy, procedures, and contract language, as required.
Mission Area Assistant CIOs will:
Ensure all USDA personnel protect PII, regardless of format or media type;
conditions: regardless of format or media type

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure all USDA personnel are familiar with and adhere to USDA privacy directives;
Ensure completion of the required privacy compliance documentation in a timely manner;
Ensure all information necessary to meet the Department’s reporting requirements regarding privacy-related USDA activities is provided to the CPO in a timely manner;
policy_statements.target: all information necessary to meet the Department’s reporting requirements regarding privacy-related USDA activities

policy_statements.source_text: Assist the CPO in reviewing USDA activities related to privacy protections, ensuring they are fully integrated into operations, that privacy incidents and privacy complaints are being addressed, and that an avenue for redress is provided, as appropriate;
conditions: as appropriate

policy_statements.source_text: Provide financial resources and other support for their respective Mission Area, agency, and staff office component Privacy Officers, Privacy Act Officers, Privacy Analysts, and other PPOCs to ensure effective implementation of all aspects of USDA privacy policy;
policy_statements.target: their respective Mission Area, agency, and staff office component Privacy Officers, Privacy Act Officers, Privacy Analysts, and other PPOCs

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that Mission Area, agency, and staff office contracts for activities that involve PII or otherwise impact the privacy of individuals include appropriate language requiring that Departmental contractors follow USDA privacy policy and this directive; and
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, and staff office contracts for activities that involve PII or otherwise impact the privacy of individuals
conditions: for activities that involve PII or otherwise impact the privacy of individuals

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure Mission Area, agency, and staff office personnel are informed and aware of the Departmental breach notification procedures as outlined in the USDA Incident Response Plan (IRP), forthcoming.
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, and staff office personnel

c. This directive establishes USDA policy and compliance with the *E-Government Act of 2002*, as amended,  44 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 3501 ; the *Confidential Information Protection and Statistical Efficiency Act of* 2002,  44 U.S.C. § 3501 ; the *Privacy Act of 1974*,  5 U.S.C. § 552  (as amended); the *Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996*,  40 U.S.C. 11101 et seq. ; and Office of Management and Budget (OMB) policies and guidance.

This policy applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices and USDA personnel working for, or on behalf of, USDA regarding the collection, use, maintenance, disclosure, deletion, destruction, or dissemination of PII, in transit and at rest, for official purposes and regarding any other activity that impacts the privacy of individuals, as determined by the USDA Senior Agency Official for Privacy (SAOP).
